item.title: - “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?” - “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for…
item.description:
- “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
- “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings.”
- “But how, venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
The destruction of delight in renewed existence,
The cessation of perception and consciousness,
The stilling of feelings —
Thus, friend, I know the release,
The escape and seclusion
For all kinds of beings.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.2
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Raṭṭhapāla: Behold this decorated image — A heap of wounds, a collection of sores, Diseased, full of lustful thoughts, Nothing stable or permanent here.…
item.description:
Elder Raṭṭhapāla:

Behold this decorated image —
A heap of wounds, a collection of sores,
Diseased, full of lustful thoughts,
Nothing stable or permanent here.

Behold this adorned appearance,
With jewels and earrings —
A skeleton covered by skin,
Made beautiful by clothes.

The feet are painted with lac and dye,
The face is smeared with powder and paste —
Enough to fool a fool,
Not one who seeks enlightenment.

The hair is curled in eight rings,
The eyes are rubbed with collyrium and rouge —
Enough to fool a fool,
Not one who seeks enlightenment.

Like a newly painted medicine box,
This foul body is adorned —
Enough to fool a fool,
Not one who seeks enlightenment.

The hunter set his trap and snare —
The wise deer does not touch the snare.
Having eaten the bait, we go away,
Leaving the trapper to mourn.

The hunter’s trap is cut —
The wise deer does not touch the snare.
Having eaten the bait, we go away,
Leaving the trapper to grieve.

From: Theragāthā 16.4
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should…
item.description:
“Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling … perception … formations … consciousness there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all consciousness should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Rādha, knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding this conscious body and all external signs, there is no ‘I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.71
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, one who delights in form delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Monks, one who delights…
item.description:
“Monks, one who delights in form delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Monks, one who delights in feeling … perception … formations … consciousness delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And, monks, one who does not delight in form does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in feeling … perception … formations … consciousness does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.29
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with…
item.description:
“Monks, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus with correct wisdom as it actually is, the mind becomes dispassionate and liberated, not grasping the defilements.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.45
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “There are these two extremes, monks, that one who has gone forth should not pursue: devotion to sensual pleasure in sensual objects — low, vulgar,…
item.description:
“There are these two extremes, monks, that one who has gone forth should not pursue: devotion to sensual pleasure in sensual objects — low, vulgar, worldly, ignoble, unbeneficial; and devotion to self-mortification — painful, ignoble, unbeneficial. Avoiding these two extremes, monks, the Middle Way has been realized by the Tathāgata, giving rise to vision, giving rise to knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna. And what, monks, is that Middle Way …? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, monks, is the Middle Way … leading to Nibbāna. This, monks, is the noble truth of suffering. Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering, association with the disliked is suffering, separation from the liked is suffering, not getting what one wants is suffering. In short, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering. This, monks, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering. It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there — that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. This, monks, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering. It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving, the abandoning and relinquishing of it, freedom from it, non-reliance. This, monks, is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view … right concentration.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 56.11
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, an untaught ordinary person does not know as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard…
item.description:
“Monks, an untaught ordinary person does not know as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Monks, a well-taught noble disciple knows as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.74
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, just as in the autumn, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, the sun, rising in the sky, dispels all darkness from…
item.description:
“Monks, just as in the autumn, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, the sun, rising in the sky, dispels all darkness from space, shines, glows, and blazes — so too, by developing and cultivating the perception of impermanence, all lust for sensual pleasures is abandoned, all lust for form is abandoned, all lust for existence is abandoned, all ignorance is abandoned, all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned. And how, monks, is the perception of impermanence developed and cultivated so that … all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned? ‘This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the cessation of form. This is feeling … this is perception … these are formations … this is consciousness, this is the arising of consciousness, this is the cessation of consciousness.’ It is when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated in this way, monks, that all lust for sensual pleasures is abandoned … all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.102
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Venerable sir, how does future rebirth occur?” “Venerable sir, when beings are shrouded by ignorance and bound by craving, delighting here and there, thus future…
item.description:
“Venerable sir, how does future rebirth occur?” “Venerable sir, when beings are shrouded by ignorance and bound by craving, delighting here and there, thus future rebirth occurs.” “Venerable sir, how does future rebirth not occur?” “Venerable sir, when ignorance is abandoned, knowledge arises, and craving is destroyed, thus future rebirth does not occur.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 43 – Mahāvedallasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Forms, sounds, tastes, odors, touches, And all phenomena — Desirable, delightful, agreeable — Thus they are called. Devas and humans in the world, Regarding them…
item.description:
Forms, sounds, tastes, odors, touches,
And all phenomena —
Desirable, delightful, agreeable —
Thus they are called.

Devas and humans in the world,
Regarding them as delightful —
Where they cease and fade away,
Devas and humans see suffering.

The noble one sees as ease
When identity view is destroyed —
The noble one sees as opposite
All the views of the world.

What others call pleasure,
The noble call suffering.
What others call suffering,
The noble know as pleasure.

See the Dhamma, hard to comprehend,
Where the ignorant are bewildered —
Darkness for the blind,
Obscurity for those who cannot see.

For the good person with open eyes,
Light is clearly seen —
Living close, they know clearly,
Skilled in the great Dhamma.

Overcome by the thirst of birth,
Swept away by the current of existence,
Subject to Māra’s control —
They do not awaken to this Dhamma.

Apart from the noble ones, no one
Awakens to this path —
The path leading to Nibbāna,
With perfect wisdom, free from defilements.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.136
📖 Read this sutta
